summary: On node1, restricted cron job scheduling to root and opsadmin only via /etc/cron.allow, verified enforcement against a third test account, then performed the mandatory single-node restart and confirmed the restriction and services survived reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS (RHEL 9.8), cron package (cronie), and existing cron.allow/cron.deny state
Created opsadmin user account on node1 (uid 1000)
Created a temporary testuser and confirmed it is denied crontab access ('not allowed to use this program')
Confirmed root and opsadmin can each create/list a crontab
Cleaned up test crontabs and removed testuser
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id and crond ActiveEnterTimestamp/active state
Issued 'shutdown -r now' backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec succeeded again, confirming connection drop then recovery
Verified crond active, /etc/cron.allow persisted with root+opsadmin, cron.deny still absent, and opsadmin can still schedule/list/remove a cron job after reboot

evidence.requirement: Only root and opsadmin can use crontab on node1 (cron.allow config)
evidence.summary: Baseline showed only cron.deny (empty) existed; created /etc/cron.allow with root and opsadmin, removed cron.deny

evidence.requirement: opsadmin account exists to be granted cron access
evidence.summary: opsadmin did not exist; created via useradd, confirmed uid 1000

evidence.requirement: Non-listed user is denied cron scheduling
evidence.summary: testuser invoking crontab as itself got 'You (testuser) are not allowed to use this program (crontab)', exit 1

evidence.requirement: root and opsadmin are allowed to schedule cron jobs
evidence.summary: Both root and opsadmin successfully created and listed a crontab entry

evidence.requirement: Cleanup of test artifacts leaving only the intended config
evidence.summary: Removed test crontabs, terminated testuser sessions, deleted testuser; confirmed testuser gone and cron.allow still root+opsadmin only

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'shutdown -r now' returned reboot_issued PID immediately
Connection dropped (timeouts/reset) during reboot, then exec succeeded again with new boot_id addc7866-17ad-4f7a-aa6f-0fec545db3ba, differing from baseline

evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery of cron service and access-control config/data
evidence.summary: crond active, /etc/cron.allow still contains only root+opsadmin, cron.deny absent, opsadmin account intact and able to create/list/remove a crontab entry post-reboot
